subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Altimeter
description: A quick, practical guide to The Altimeter.

hook.text: Knowing how high you are sounds simple. In a plane, it's surprisingly tricky to measure.

buildup.text: Altimeters measure air pressure. As you climb, pressure drops in a predictable way.

discovery.text: A barometric altimeter converts that pressure reading into altitude—feet above sea level.

twist.text: But air pressure changes with weather. A wrong barometric setting can cause altitude errors of hundreds of feet.

climax.text: Pilots constantly update their altimeter setting from air traffic control to stay accurate.

punchline.text: Your altitude is only as accurate as your weather data.

quiz.question: How do barometric altimeters determine altitude?
options: Measuring air pressure changes with height
